RCT involving elderly patients with recurrent depression randomized to 3-year maintenance nortriptyline at two different plasma levels. Meets criteria.
RCT involving outpatients aged 65+ who responded to acute citalopram and were randomized to maintenance citalopram vs placebo. Meets all criteria.

RCT evaluating maintenance cognitive therapy vs pharmacotherapy for recurrent depression. Age group is not explicitly specified as 60+, but conservative screening warrants inclusion for full-text verification.

Methodological paper comparing meta-analysis techniques using cancer survival data. Not an RCT on depression.
RCT comparing MBCT with maintenance antidepressants for relapse prevention. Age group is not explicitly specified as 60+, but conservative screening warrants inclusion for full-text verification.

Systematic overview and meta-analysis of antidepressant continuation trials. Not a primary RCT.

This is an RCT evaluating maintenance Interpersonal Psychotherapy (IPT) vs supportive clinical management in remitted depressed elderly patients. Participants were aged 60+ (elderly), had successfully achieved remission from depression, and were randomized to maintenance treatment. The study examines recurrence rates and time to recurrence, which directly addresses the review objective of preventing relapse/recurrence of depression in older people.

This is not a primary RCT study. The abstract reads as a review/commentary discussing the potential of psychotherapy for elderly depression and noting the need for further evaluation. It references evidence from other RCTs but does not present original trial data. Does not meet the RCT criterion.

This is a Cochrane review (indicated by cochranelibrary.com), not a primary RCT. The objectives state it aims to examine efficacy of antidepressant classes for treating depression in elderly patients aged 55+, but it is a systematic review itself, not an original trial. Additionally, it focuses on acute treatment efficacy rather than continuation/maintenance treatment after remission.

This is an observational population-based study examining antidepressant prescribing patterns in Lombardy, Italy. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate treatment efficacy for continuation/maintenance of depression. The study uses administrative database records to calculate prevalence of antidepressant use.

This is an RCT where 58 elderly subjects remitted from major depression received continuation nortriptyline treatment for 16 weeks, then were randomly assigned to nortriptyline maintenance therapy or placebo for up to 2 years. Participants were aged 60+ (elderly), successfully treated (remitted), and randomized to maintenance treatment. The study examines relapse and recurrence outcomes, directly relevant to the review objective.

This appears to be a Cochrane review (indicated by cochranelibrary.com), not a primary RCT. The abstract is extremely brief, containing only background and objectives sections typical of a review protocol or published review. It does not present original trial data.

This is a community-based prospective observational study, not an RCT. It examines the relationship between persistent depressive symptoms and functional disability in elderly persons from the Cardiovascular Health Study. There is no randomization to treatment interventions.

This is a systematic literature review informed by an expert panel, not a primary RCT. It appraises publications on community-based interventions for depression in older adults and rates their effectiveness. It does not present original trial data.

This is an RCT (randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled maintenance trial) involving 130 older adults aged 65+ with recently remitted major depression. Participants were randomized to maintenance antidepressant pharmacotherapy plus donepezil or maintenance antidepressant pharmacotherapy plus placebo. The study examines recurrence of depression over 2 years of maintenance treatment. While donepezil is a cholinesterase inhibitor rather than a traditional antidepressant or psychological therapy, it is being tested as an augmentation strategy in maintenance treatment of depression, and the study directly addresses recurrence prevention in remitted elderly patients. Conservative inclusion warranted given the maintenance treatment focus and RCT design.

This study describes recruitment strategies for a dietary intervention trial (The FIT study) examining diet and immune function, not depression treatment. It is not an RCT of antidepressant or psychological therapy for continuation/maintenance of depression. The focus is entirely on recruitment methodology.

This is an RCT (2x2 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial) involving patients older than 59 years (average age 67) with recurrent major depression who were fully recovered after acute and continuation treatment. Participants were randomized to 4 maintenance therapy conditions: nortriptyline alone, IPT alone, combination, or placebo. The study examines recurrence of major depressive episodes over 3 years, directly addressing the review objective of preventing relapse/recurrence in older people.

This is a methodological paper describing the development and limitations of a rating scale for measuring depression symptoms. It is not an RCT of treatment interventions for continuation/maintenance of depression in older people.

While this is an RCT involving older people (65+) with depression, it does not meet the continuation/maintenance criterion. Participants had active depression at baseline (Geriatric Mental State diagnosis of depression) and were randomized to acute treatment (CBT vs talking control vs treatment as usual). The study examines acute treatment effectiveness, not continuation/maintenance treatment after successful remission. The review specifically requires studies of people 'successfully treated for an episode of depression' who are then randomized to continuation/maintenance treatment.

This is a methodological paper describing the development and validation of a 27-item therapy rating scale to evaluate therapists' use of maintenance treatments (IPT-M vs Medication Clinic). It is not an RCT evaluating treatment efficacy for preventing relapse/recurrence of depression. The study focuses on psychometric properties of a rating instrument.
